candidate.title: BS-Seq / Bisulfite-seq / WGBS
candidate.scope: Shared architecture of the assigned middle poster row labeled BS-Seq / Bisulfite-seq / WGBS: genomic DNA shearing, bisulfite conversion and the PCR base-conversion inset, ending in DNA. The yellow-ring overview icon is descriptive; the inset magnifies base chemistry rather than splitting a sample. Adjacent SMDB and EpiGnome/HELP-Seq rows are outside this extraction. The three names designate the grouped whole-genome bisulfite-sequencing depiction, not proof that all implementations have identical library preparation.

operations.label: Shear DNA
operations.description: Fragment the input genomic DNA into shorter DNA pieces while retaining the depicted cytosine modifications.
operations.information_effect: Genomic sequence context and pre-existing modification positions are retained on individual fragments; no enrichment or compartment partition is drawn.

evidence.locator: Middle row, Shear DNA arrow and shorter blue DNA lines retaining red dots

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion (inset: Bisulfite)
operations.description: Treat the sheared genomic DNA so unmodified cytosines become uracils while the depicted modified cytosine resists conversion. The inset illustrates this transformation on the same route.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite-dependent conversion distinguishes susceptible unmodified C from the protected modified C in the cartoon.
operations.information_effect: Original cytosine conversion susceptibility becomes a C-versus-U base distinction on the genomic fragments, retaining sequence context. The catalogue explicitly warns that standard bisulfite conversion cannot distinguish 5mC from 5hmC, so protection is not uniquely specific to 5mC. Conversion also reduces sequence complexity and can make genomic alignment difficult.

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplify the bisulfite-converted DNA; the inset represents U as T in the resulting DNA while the protected site remains C.
operations.information_effect: PCR converts the U-containing template information into T-containing DNA sequence; originally protected cytosine positions remain read as C. Aligned C/T observations at reference cytosines support single-base conversion-resistance calls and, across reads, estimated site methylation fractions. The carrier is genomic DNA sequence, not an antibody, probe product or directly sequenced chemical mark. These calls inherit bisulfite specificity and conversion limitations.

The matching secondary collection page explicitly groups BS-Seq/Bisulfite-seq or WGBS and labels the upper matching schematic as an overview of BS-Seq. At this shared schematic scope it supports fragment→conversion→PCR preparation. This does not assert complete MethylC-seq/BS-Seq protocol identity.

All three supplied method references and all three methods have explicit paper assessments, with full-text architecture support distinguished from bibliographic identification.
